	In particular,

		T(\varepsilon):=\min\{k \mid \|\nabla G(x_k,y_k)\|\leq \varepsilon \}.

Note that the widely used metrics for convex-concave minimax problems such as the min-max value or the distance to the set of optimal solutions of the min-max problem are not applicable in nonconvex cases.
	For the latter cases we call $(x_k,y_k)$ an $\varepsilon$-stationary point of $f(x,y)$ if $ \|
abla G(x_k,y_k)\|\leq \varepsilon$ with $
abla G(x_k,y_k)$ being defined as in Definition ef{sec:2:def1:G}, which has been widely used as the optimality measure, e.g., \cite{Lin2020,Lu}. In the absence of constraints, $ \| 
abla G(x_k,y_k)\| \leq \varepsilon$ reduces to the standard condition $ \|
abla_{x} f(x_k ,y_k)\|\leq \varepsilon $ and $\|
abla_{y} f(x_k ,y_k)\|\leq \varepsilon$ for unconstrained problems. The vector  $
